key_insight: A dislocation-informed constitutive model links BCC metal flow to temperature and strain rate while specifying how structural resistance and competing kinetic mechanisms combine.
engineering_relevance: The model supports mechanism-based prediction of strength and creep across temperature and loading-rate regimes, with potential value for alloy design.
method: Develop a temperature-dependent screw-dislocation mobility law combining thermal activation and relativistic effects.
Run discrete dislocation dynamics tension and compression simulations with varied initial dislocation densities.
Derive a unified constitutive model connecting microscopic mechanisms to continuum plastic flow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports bottom-up simulations that quantify the crossover from thermal activation to phonon drag and explain anomalous thermal hardening.
watch_item: Experimental validation and quantitative prediction errors are not reported in the abstract, leaving practical transferability to specific BCC alloys uncertain.
paper_title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
